SMTO-HTTP-0018 — SMTO couldn't match this sign-in to its request

GUID: 78f02190-d86e-4e6b-be23-dd87760325ef
Slug: http-oauth-invalid-state
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The web service sent back a sign-in that doesn't match the one SMTO is waiting for, for example from an older or already-used sign-in link. SMTO ignored it for your safety and didn't connect.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close any browser tabs left over from earlier sign-in attempts for this service. An old tab can send back a sign-in that no longer matches what SMTO is waiting for.
  2. Ask SMTO in the conversation to connect to the service again, then use only the newest Open authorization page link to sign in. Each link carries a one-time code that matches only the current sign-in request.
  3. If SMTO was restarted while you were signing in, start the sign-in again from the previous step. A restart forgets the pending sign-in, so an older link can't be completed.

What success looks like

  • The sign-in prompt disappears and SMTO continues the task using the service.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Never put passwords, codes or access tokens in the conversation, screenshots or error reports.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An OAuth authorization-code callback had no matching pending transaction, or its state value did not match the transaction's state.

What this means

  • An authorization-code callback has no matching transaction or its state fails constant-time comparison with the owned state. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • An authorization-code callback has no matching transaction or its state fails constant-time comparison with the owned state.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect transaction ownership and callback association; never bypass the state comparison.

How to fix it

  • OAuth2.prepare_session raises this when an authorization-code callback arrives but the flow has no pending authorization transaction or the callback state fails secrets.compare_digest against it (a stale or reused link, or state lost after a Server restart). Discard the stale state and start a new authorization flow; never reuse an old authorization URL.
  • Discard stale OAuth state and start a fresh supported authorization flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh callback matches its own unexpired transaction and accepted state.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
